What Apple Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) is — and what your listing may claim

Apple ships Hearing Aid Compatibility under Settings → Accessibility → Hearing → Hearing Aid Compatibility (also reachable via Settings → Accessibility → Hearing Devices on some iOS versions). When enabled, the device optimizes phone-call audio for hearing-aid wearers using telecoil coupling or MFi hearing aids in HAC mode. Western indie listings often show one or more of these surfaces on the US product page. AppLocale covers paste-ready zh-Hans copy for whichever your screenshots and description already claim:

  • Hearing Aid Compatibility toggle (助听器兼容性) — master switch that enables HAC mode for clearer call audio with compatible hearing aids. Gallery frames may show the Hearing settings branch or a "Works with Hearing Aid Compatibility" badge.
  • MFi hearing aids & HAC mode (Made for iPhone 助听器 / MFi 助听器) — marketing that emphasizes Made for iPhone hearing-aid compatibility for phone calls, VoIP sessions, or telecoil-equipped hearing hardware. Screenshot overlays often show MFi logo art, HAC mode setup walkthroughs, or hearing-aid-compatible call demos.
  • Telecoil-compatible phone calls (听力设备) — when your English listing explains that call audio routes cleanly to telecoil-equipped hearing aids with reduced buzzing or interference. zh-Hans copy should use 听力设备 or 助听器 only when your US page already claims telecoil call compatibility — not as a generic "better audio" synonym.
  • HAC ratings & compatibility badges — M3/T3, M4/T4, or "Hearing Aid Compatible" callouts when your US listing cites FCC HAC ratings or hearing-aid-compatible phone hardware. Match what your gallery actually shows.
  • HAC-aware call workflows in your app — VoIP, telephony, audiology, or hearing-assist apps that respect system HAC mode during calls. Screenshot overlays often show HAC badges on call UI, hearing-aid-compatible dialer screens, or settings walkthroughs under 辅助功能听力.

Your gallery may lead with a Hearing Aid Compatibility settings toggle on one frame and an in-app VoIP call with HAC badge on the next. zh-Hans caption lines should name the correct surface per frame — an HAC toggle is not a Hearing Devices pairing sheet, not a Headphone Accommodations EQ graph, and not a Live Listen microphone badge unless that is what the screenshot shows.

HAC-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Hearing-aid compatibility marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe HAC workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

HAC mode vs Hearing Devices hub vs MFi pairing

US pages use "Hearing Aid Compatibility", "HAC mode", or "telecoil compatible." China storefront copy often uses 助听器兼容性 for Apple's HAC toggle, 助听器 for hearing aids, 听力设备 for hearing hardware, Made for iPhone 助听器 for Apple's MFi hearing-aid branding, and MFi 助听器 for compatibility badges — depending on whether you mean HAC call mode, telecoil routing, or broader Hearing Devices pairing. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope and avoids conflating HAC with the full Hearing Devices hub when your screenshots show only the HAC toggle.

HAC vs Headphone Accommodations vs Headphone Notifications

Hearing Aid Compatibility (助听器兼容性) optimizes call audio for telecoil-equipped hearing aids. Headphone Accommodations (耳机调节) tunes frequency EQ for AirPods or wired headphones. Headphone Notifications and Headphone Safety warn about loud headphone exposure — different surfaces under Hearing and Audio & Visual. Do not reuse 耳机调节 or loud-sound vocabulary on HAC call frames unless that is what the screenshot depicts.

HAC vs Live Listen vs Closed Captions

HAC mode improves phone-call audio routing to hearing aids. Live Listen (实时收听) streams iPhone microphone audio to AirPods or hearing devices for conversation amplification. Closed Captions + SDH (隐藏式字幕) displays embedded media caption tracks. Each Hearing surface has distinct screenshot vocabulary — match what your English listing and gallery actually show.

Telecoil vs generic Bluetooth audio

Telecoil-compatible call marketing describes hearing-aid induction coupling for phone audio — not generic Bluetooth A2DP streaming to headphones or AirPods unless your US listing already claims that accurately. AppLocale rewrites from your source claims — we do not invent telecoil support your gallery does not show.
